newsitem.title: USA: S.E. Asia seen key to future US pork export market.
newsitem.headline: S.E. Asia seen key to future US pork export market.

text.p: South East Asia could be a lucrative export market for U.S. pork in the future, said Bob Ruggles, president of the National Pork Producers Council.

"Let's look seriously at S.E. Asia. Double digit growth rates in Taiwan, China, Singapore and South Korea, coupled with the economic stagnation of Europe has created a whole new world economic architecture," said Ruggles, in remarks for delivery at the NPPC's National Pork Industry Forum.
He noted that the World Bank was forecasting that by 2020, nine of the 15 strongest economies in the world would be in S.E. Asia, with China likely to be the strongest economy.
Ruggles said the U.S. had been rising on the table of world pork exporters and was currently second.
"We are dramatically shifting from a domestic market orientation to an international focus," he said.

Ruggles said there was a future for small- or medium-size producers as intellectual capabilities become more important than hard assets. He noted in virtually every industry the comparative advantage based on economy of scale was declining.
"Size and scale in tomorrow's world will be less important, speed and responsiveness to the market will win the day," Ruggles said.

"For those who say that only the big will survive in the coming years are assuming that change is linear--that tomorrow will be a straight-line extrapolation of the past. That's yesterday's news," he said.
